disputed.finding: The report is framed in the present tense and says the first stocktake is "in 2023" without noting that it concluded at COP28 (Dec 2023) and that the second is due in 2028, as of Nov 2026. This is outdated for a report dated Nov 2026, though the notes themselves lack it.
disputed.objection: The notes do not address the report date or later stocktake developments, so this is a potentially valid timeliness concern but not one settled by the research notes.

disputed.finding: “In practical terms, the Paris Agreement creates a cycle like this...” The cycle is implied by the provisions, but this synthesized step-by-step sequence is not directly stated in the sources.
disputed.objection: The four-step cycle is a straightforward synthesis of Articles 4(9), 14(2) and 14(3) as quoted in the notes, so calling it unsupported is overstated.

disputed.finding: Article 4(9) is quoted with an ellipsis after ‘every five years ...’ but the draft does not clarify the full sentence. As written, it may obscure that Article 4(9) also says the NDC will be informed by the outcomes of the global stocktake.
disputed.objection: The draft's quote includes the stocktake clause after the ellipsis, so the point is not obscured; the finding is overstated.

disputed.finding: The draft says the stocktake occurs ‘on the same broad timetable as NDC submission.’ The notes support five-year cycles for both, but the first stocktake was in 2023, while the NDC cycle is every five years; the alignment is not exact in timing for all rounds.
disputed.objection: The draft says 'same broad timetable', which hedges the claim, and the notes give both cycles as five-yearly, so the objection about inexact timing is speculative.

disputed.finding: “The direction is one-way: adjustments are contemplated for enhancing ambition, not weakening it.” The cited Article 4(11) says adjust with a view to enhancing ambition, so the broad point is right, but the draft could be read as an absolute legal prohibition on any other form of adjustment; the notes do not support that stronger claim.
disputed.objection: The draft only says adjustments are contemplated for enhancing ambition, which matches the quoted text; the claim of an absolute prohibition is a reader's overreading.
